slides.narration: Chapter 2: The First Distinction. Omega examines itself — and in that act, the first structure is born.

When Omega examines itself, something unprecedented happens. There is now an examiner and something being examined. These are not two separate things — they are two roles played by the same wholeness. But the distinction between them is real.

Imagine two mirrors placed face to face. Each reflects the other, creating an infinite corridor of reflections. This is the structure Omega creates when it looks inward — observer and observed reflecting each other endlessly.

lines: The only shape with no preferred direction
slides.narration: What shape does this take? A sphere — the only shape where every direction is equivalent. No point is special, no axis is preferred. It is the geometric expression of perfect self-reference.

Every sphere carries an intrinsic ratio: its circumference divided by its diameter. This ratio — which we call circle-pi, written as the symbol sun-circle — equals pi. It was not chosen. It was not derived. It is simply what you get when the first distinction has the shape of a sphere.

Three axioms emerge from this single act: Axiom 2, that Omega examines itself. Axiom 3, that the examination is spherical. And Axiom 4, that the sphere carries the ratio circle-pi. From nothing, geometry is born.
